rows.what the ink shows: A compressed initial u-like cup runs into a long low connecting stroke, followed by the steep descending f stroke and a distinct raised final t before the separate initial stroke of fermée; this is the abbreviated uniformt.

In the word after fonction, the heavy cancellation covers most of the letter bodies. A short downward tick, low curved join, small upright nub and final rounded return remain below or across the deletion; they do not recover the whole continue sequence with enough independence.

The cancelled word has two taller initial remnants above the strike and a separate dot around its middle, but its connecting letters and ending are covered by thick ink. These remnants are compatible with définie without distinguishing the complete word.

The inserted first word has an initial upright hook, a long low join, a tall medial l and a low ending, followed by the raised initial d and flattened ending of dans. The following word is one connected low bowl and long flat terminal hook, matching the clear un before C_0(M) on this page. It lacks the separate upright initial s and middle dot/oval visible in the clear son after the first underlined b. This supports un rather than son. The last group has an initial c-like turn and a high right-hand terminal with a separate small insertion above it, but its middle letters do not securely establish complément.
After M and its comma, a low initial a joins a tall l and rounded o; the middle is rubbed by a pale diagonal smear, but the following r-like upright and final open s remain visible before the comma.

Under the cancellation the word begins with a small open c, has a crossed tall t and a separate i dot, and ends in several linked low rounded strokes beneath the ruling. These surviving strokes support continue.

The long cancelled word to the right of continue retains shallow curved strokes beneath the ruling, a downward turn near its early part and an open final bowl. The deletion obscures the distinctive central letters and any reliable accent, so supérieure cannot be established from the surviving ink.
The inserted letter before the membership sign has a tall slanting stroke, a lower closed loop and two short crossing strokes. Its looped descender and cross-strokes identify f.

The deletion crosses virtually the entire x-height. A low initial rise and short trough survive at the left, and a tall narrow loop near the right is followed by a short terminal baseline stroke. These are compatible with the proposed word but the middle letters, including the claimed b, cannot be separated from the strike.

After the visible qui est, a small hooked onset, a deep p-like downstroke, a crossed t-like ascender and a taller loop remain. Farther right a second descender, an upper dot or accent and a low final bowl survive. The straight deletion obliterates most connecting letters and the boundary between the proposed words; these survivors do not independently fix the entire phrase.

The compact open curved sign and following short separated mark at the right end resemble the same-page unmarked qui: its q has an open descending loop and a long horizontal continuation, followed by a short i-stroke/dot. This makes the earlier membership-like segmentation insecure; no additional membership sign is independently visible. The following tall rising glyph has a hooked low foot and a short separate horizontal stroke, but its exact alignment with the unmarked underlined a is not secure. There are no distinguishable proposed prose words between these compact forms, yet the boundary is too ambiguous to assign a definite blank span or an empty replacement.

A heavy outer stroke rises into a right-facing upper hook and rounds into a lower right tip, forming C over a thinner old closed/diagonal loop. At the lower right, one small raised dot/caret and one low hooked i-stroke are visible. The inspected whitespace after that stroke contains no separate lower zero, unlike the second occurrence.

The darker outer upper and lower arcs form a right-open C over the thinner closed D-like remnant. The subscript has a separate raised dot and low i-bowl, followed farther right and lower by a small bent oval/zero stroke; the extra lower mark is visible here.

After the open parenthesis, a tall narrow d-like upright with a small lower return survives, followed by a dot-like low trace and one elongated shallow curve. The heavy straight cancellation merges the upper bodies of the remaining letters; the separate terminal c seen in the clear same-page donc does not survive distinctly here. Retain the proposed word as uncertain.

Following une, a low horizontal curved run is visible beneath the cancellation, then two rising loop/stem forms and further short separated low curves. These are compatible with parts of sous-algèbre, but the deletion line passes through the letter junctions and the proposed g, accent and final letter sequence cannot be separated confidently at 4×.

After un, the canceled word has a narrow down-and-back loop below the line, an extended shallow bowl, a short rising diagonal through the strike and a small detached low curve near its end. Most letter bodies are merged into the dark cancellation; the visible fragments do not independently establish the full compact sequence.

The next canceled word retains an upward slanting stroke at its left, a deep pointed downstroke near the middle and a short diagonal/upstroke cluster near its right. The oval bodies and intervening humps are hidden along the cancellation, so the full quelconque reading remains uncertain despite the surviving descender.

Between de and the period is one tall rounded arch with a left baseline foot and a right outward foot. The arch survives above the cancellation and contains no second peak or central joining stroke. Its outline matches the clear Ω higher on this same page; the page's M forms instead have several tall dark strokes and a central loop.

The capital U retains two tall oblique uprights and a lower joining turn. Its subscript has a long phi descender and a small lower k-shaped hooked branch to the right. Farther right an open rounded membership stroke is visible above and below the strike, followed by a small a-shaped arch and the separate low horizontal underline, though additional cancellation strokes cross the formula.
